name: Twelve Patients (Teaching Set)
description: A constructed 12-person trial: 6 treatment, 6 placebo, with 5 and 2 improving. Small enough to deal out as cards and count by hand.
studyDescription: Twelve people were randomly assigned, six to a new treatment and six to a placebo, and each was recorded as improved or not. Five of the six on the treatment improved; two of the six on the placebo did. This is a constructed teaching set, not real data.

variableDescriptions.group: Which arm the person was randomly assigned to: Treatment or Placebo.

sourceDetail: Constructed teaching set (not real data), sized for the “What does a shuffle show?” demo. Twelve observations is small enough to deal as cards and count by eye, and with both margins fixed the difference in proportions takes exactly SIX achievable values (±5/6, ±1/2, ±1/6), with exact probabilities 7/924, 105/924 and 350/924 either side of zero. Observed difference 5/6 − 2/6 = 0.5; one-sided permutation p = 112/924 = 0.1212 (enumerated, not simulated). Row order is a fixed shuffle (seed 7); the statistic does not depend on it.
context: Did the treatment really help, or could a shuffle of these same twelve people produce a gap this big?
nullClaim: the treatment and the placebo make no difference
